summary: Iter 5 (Real Starting Balance): wrote /app/backend/tests/test_iteration5_start_equity.py (7 tests) + UI check on dashboard with a fresh TEST_ user. 6/7 backend tests pass. PnlChart no longer shows hardcoded $10,000 — new TEST_ user sees 'START $0.00 / NOW $0.00 / +$0.00'. refresh_live_equity unit test verified first call sets start_equity=8.94 & start_ts, second call with equity 9.5 preserves start_equity=8.94 and only updates live_equity. /api/bot/reset correctly sets start_equity=live_equity (or null when none). /api/exchange/disconnect clears start_equity/start_ts/live_equity. /api/bot/pnl correctly filters points with ts<start_ts when start_ts set. One real backend bug surfaced: GET /api/bot/state does NOT include the start_equity key for a brand-new user because DEFAULT_BOT lacks the field and bot_view only spreads existing keys. UI gracefully handles it via `bot?.start_equity ?? data[0]?.equity ?? 0`, but the API contract in the spec is violated. Also found a race-condition bug in get_bot (duplicate key error on concurrent first requests). Did NOT touch user_id 6ad0c885f4fa421663189000 (real OKX customer).

minor.issue: `start_equity` key is missing from response for a brand-new user (DEFAULT_BOT does not include start_equity, so bot_view's spread does not emit it). Spec requires start_equity to be present as null. Fix: add `start_equity: None, start_ts: None` to DEFAULT_BOT (engine.py) OR force-include them in bot_view (server.py).

minor.endpoint: GET /api/bot/state and others on first hit
minor.issue: Race condition in get_bot (server.py): when the dashboard fires several parallel requests for a user that has no bot doc yet, each coroutine passes the `if bot` check and attempts insert_one, causing `pymongo.errors.DuplicateKeyError: E11000 ... bots index: user_id_1`. Visible in backend.err.log and surfaces as 500 responses on 1-2 of the initial calls (observed in browser console). Fix: use upsert ($setOnInsert) or wrap insert in try/except DuplicateKeyError and re-fetch.

action_items: Include start_equity (and start_ts) keys in GET /api/bot/state response — add to DEFAULT_BOT or explicitly in bot_view so new users get `start_equity: null` as per spec.

Fix race condition in server.get_bot: initial concurrent requests race to insert the bot doc and trigger DuplicateKeyError 500s. Use `db.bots.update_one({user_id}, {\"$setOnInsert\": doc}, upsert=True)` then find_one.
critical_code_review_comments: engine.refresh_live_equity re-reads start_equity from DB before setting (`fresh.get('start_equity')`), which correctly prevents overwriting after the first non-zero equity — good.
bot_reset uses `bot.get('live_equity') or None` so a stale 0.0 live_equity would become None — intended behavior; verified.
server.get_bot has a TOCTOU race (described above).
PnlChart handles missing bot.start_equity gracefully via `?? data[0]?.equity ?? 0`, keeping UI resilient even if backend omits the key.

All 7 should pass. Real OKX user 6ad0c885f4fa421663189000 was not touched (read-only requirement respected — no API calls made against that account).
rca_of_the_issue: start_equity missing from /api/bot/state: DEFAULT_BOT dict in engine.py does not define `start_equity`/`start_ts`, and bot_view in server.py only iterates over existing bot keys. For a user who has never connected an exchange, `refresh_live_equity` is never called (early-returns on missing creds), so `start_equity` is never written to the doc and therefore absent in the API response. Reproduction: register a new user → GET /api/bot/state → response has no `start_equity` key. Mitigation: add `start_equity: None, start_ts: None` to DEFAULT_BOT so the field is always serialized.
